newsitem.title: USA: African elephant protection bill introduced.
newsitem.headline: African elephant protection bill introduced.

text.p: A bill to help protect African elephants from poachers was introduced on Wednesday by the chairman of a U.S. House of Representatives panel.
Resources Committee Chairman Don Young said the bill would authorise up to $5 million a year in federal funds for the African Elephant Conservation Act.
It would be matched by money from private groups like the African Wildlife Foundation, Safari Club International and the World Wildlife Fund and used to help African nations fight poachers.

"This historic conservation act is vital to our efforts to save the African elephant from illegal poachers who have slaughtered these magnificent animals simply for their ivory tusks," Young, an Alaska Republican, said in a statement.
He said the number of African elephants had been reduced from 1.3 million to 700,000 since 1979, mainly by poachers.
Young said the act had helped fund 48 elephant conservation projects in 17 African countries since it was passed in 1988.
The bill was co-sponsored by Representative Randy Cunningham, a California Republican.
